prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: base editing as a single-achievement prize credited to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli. The discovery is a defined chemical step on DNA, a deaminase positioned by a programmable nickase to convert one base, with the cell's own repair completing the edit and no double-strand break. The chemistry is the new part where it matters most: no natural adenine deaminase acting on DNA existed, so the TadA enzyme had to be evolved to do it, which is Gaudelli's contribution, and the cytosine editor is Komor's. Both are mechanistically quantified, replicated in very many laboratories and organisms, and in patients. From my own field, a tool that changes a base without provoking the damage response that double-strand breaks trigger is a real advance for genome maintenance work, because it lets one ask about nucleobase chemistry without a confounding repair pathway. I weigh this as measured evidence of independent reproduction and mechanism, not as opening support.
statement.case_against: The strongest objections stay as in round 1. Base editing sits close to the 2020 prize and some members will read it as a follow-on. Durability, bystander edits and off-target deamination are still being measured. The attribution is not airtight, because Kondo and Nishida reported Target-AID at about the same time and I cannot verify the priority record from the material in front of me. A trio that seats two trainees is a harder allocation to defend than Liu alone, and the chair is right that the citation cannot lean on the trainees' papers if they are excluded. I also accept that a single-part prize leaves out the degradation field, which several colleagues value, and that is a cost of my choice, not a point in its favour.

responses.point: Aili pairs base editing credited to Liu alone with PROTACs credited to Crews and Deshaies, and names the Liu-only credit as an attribution compromise, with a single-part base-editing trio as the fallback if Liu-only is indefensible.
responses.response: I agree with Aili's own reading of the weakness: the pairing is arithmetic that fits three seats and drops the two people who wrote the decisive base-editor papers. You named the trio as your fallback, and I would ask that the committee treat that as the primary question, not the reserve. On the second part, I do not see a quantitative case that a PROTAC concept from 2001 is mature when no PROTAC is an approved drug and the cereblon glue lineage has its own claim. I would not choose a two-part prize if it requires trimming a part I think is well supported to make room for one I think is early.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, proposes Liu alone for base editing with Crews and Deshaies for degradation, and in his own case against says Komor and Gaudelli wrote decisive first-author papers and that Kondo and Nishida reported Target-AID independently.
responses.response: In round 1 I wrote that Linke placed a Liu, Komor and Gaudelli configuration first. His file in fact proposes Liu alone, so I correct that. I still agree with his central point that the citation must be about the chemistry of base conversion and not about genome editing. But the exclusion he lists in his own against-case is the one I find hardest to defend: the evolved deaminase is the new chemistry, and Gaudelli's adenine editor is the clearest example of it. If the citation names the deaminase step, then the person who evolved it belongs in the credit, not only in the citation text. On Target-AID, the chair's question is the right one and I would defer to documented dates, but a different architecture reported close in time shapes the wording more than the names unless the record shows an earlier general demonstration.

responses.point: Aqvist holds a two-part prize of Liu alone and Crews and Deshaies, defends Liu alone as intellectual originator with an engineering programme, and offers to shift the degradation part to Handa if the glue lineage is the mature core.
responses.response: I accept that Liu directed the programme and is its originator. I do not think that settles credit when the decisive experiments for both editor classes were done by two named individuals who are first authors on the founding papers. Your own against-case concedes this. I note that your offer to move to Handa shows the degradation part is itself unsettled on names, and that is the point where I find single-part base editing more defensible than a pair whose second half you are willing to reallocate.

responses.point: Somfai presses that the new chemistry in base editing is largely protein engineering and directed evolution on top of the 2020 CRISPR platform, and proposes pairing it with Buchwald and Hartwig for C-N coupling.
responses.response: I take the directed-evolution objection seriously, but it does not remove the chemistry. The reaction that matters, hydrolytic deamination of a defined base inside a protein-DNA complex, and the outcome, a point change without a double-strand break, are not in the 2020 citation. Evolving an enzyme to carry out a reaction that no natural enzyme performs on that substrate is a chemical achievement in the same sense as many past enzyme prizes. On B003, I have no doubt about maturity or attribution, and I would support it as a stand-alone prize. I do not see a unifying theme in a pairing, and I would prefer the committee choose one coherent citation to a mixed one. I do not think the B003 pairing is better than my single-part trio, because the Liu-only credit it relies on has the same weakness.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) have a documented priority that should change the credited names; I cannot verify dates and the reports from the shortlist alone are insufficient.

Whether the committee accepts two trainees as laureates in a prize led by a principal investigator, or insists on Liu alone; I would accept a Liu-only credit if the citation text names the deaminase step and the committee records why, but I judge it second best.

Whether the committee views base editing as distinct from the 2020 prize; I think the double-strand-break-free chemical step is distinct, but I cannot show that this view will hold with the full committee.

Whether a PROTAC concept is mature enough without an approved drug, and whether the PROTAC or cereblon glue lineage is the right core; if base editing does not reach majority I am unsure whether degradation or sequencing is the better fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict to disclose, and no change from round 1. My work on dNTP pools and replication fidelity is in a neighbouring area of nucleic-acid biochemistry, but I have no collaboration, institutional tie or funding relationship with any credited name on the shortlist, and no recusal is needed.
